issue.title: redfish: supervisor-proc-exit-listener cannot read CONFIG_DB in bridge-mode container (autorestart broken)

failure.body:
### Description

The `supervisor-proc-exit-listener` inside the `redfish` container cannot read CONFIG_DB, so it never propagates critical-process exits into container teardown. `feature autorestart` for redfish is effectively broken.

### Root cause

`redfish` is the only SONiC container that runs with `--net=bridge` instead of `--net=host` (see [`files/build_templates/docker_image_ctl.j2#L699-L704`](https://github.com/sonic-net/sonic-buildimage/blob/master/files/build_templates/docker_image_ctl.j2#L699-L704)):

```jinja
{%- if docker_container_name == "redfish" %}
    NET="bridge"
{%- else %}
    NET="host"
{%- endif %}
```

Bridge mode is used so that `-p <IP>:443:18080` can remap the external HTTPS port (bmcweb listens on :18080 inside the container).

Consequence: inside the redfish container, `<IP>:6379` does not reach the host redis. `ConfigDBConnector().connect()` fails with:

```
RuntimeError: Unable to connect to redis - Connection refused
```

The listener in [`dockers/docker-sonic-redfish/supervisord.conf`](https://github.com/sonic-net/sonic-buildimage/blob/master/dockers/docker-sonic-redfish/supervisord.conf) is:

```
command=/usr/local/bin/supervisor-proc-exit-listener --container-name redfish
```

Without `-s/--use-unix-socket-path`, it uses TCP-mode `ConfigDBConnector`, which cannot reach redis in bridge-mode netns. When a critical process (e.g. `sonic-dbus-bridge`) exits:

1. Listener receives `PROCESS_STATE_EXITED`.
2. `get_autorestart_state()` → `connect()` raises → caught → returns `""`.
3. `"" != "enabled"` → listener does **not** send `SIGTERM` to supervisord.
4. Supervisord's own `autorestart=true` respawns the critical process in place.
5. Container never stops. `sonic-mgmt` `autorestart/test_container_autorestart.py::test_containers_autorestart[...-redfish]` fails with "Failed to stop container 'redfish'".

The other 25 SONiC containers using this listener are unaffected: they run on `--net=host`, so `<IP>:6379` resolves to the host redis instance.

### Environment

- Platform: SONiC BMC on Chipmunk (aspeed-arm64)
- Image: `sonic-aspeed-arm64-20260810.06.bin`
- Reproducible on `sonic-net/sonic-buildimage` master (config unchanged since PR #26003).

### Reproduction

```bash
# on the DUT, all-defaults deploy-mg config
sudo config feature autorestart redfish enabled

# confirm listener can't reach redis
docker exec redfish python3 -c 'from swsscommon import swsscommon; c=swsscommon.ConfigDBConnector(); c.connect()'
# -> RuntimeError: Unable to connect to redis - Connection refused

# kill a critical process
docker exec redfish kill -9 $(docker exec redfish supervisorctl pid sonic-dbus-bridge)

# expected: container tears down within a few seconds
# actual: supervisord respawns the process; container stays up indefinitely
```

### Proposed fix

Add `--use-unix-socket-path` to the listener command in `dockers/docker-sonic-redfish/supervisord.conf`. The redfish container already bind-mounts `/var/run/redis:/var/run/redis:rw`, so `redis.sock` is available.

```diff
-command=/usr/local/bin/supervisor-proc-exit-listener --container-name redfish
+command=/usr/local/bin/supervisor-proc-exit-listener --container-name redfish --use-unix-socket-path
```

### Validation

Applied the one-line fix on a running Chipmunk BMC DUT:

- Before: `docker exec redfish kill -9 <dbus-bridge pid>` → supervisord respawned in place; container up 2h+.
- After: `docker exec redfish kill -9 <dbus-bridge pid>` → container exited within 30s (`systemd[1]: redfish.service: Deactivated successfully`); systemd restarted the service; new container came up clean.

PR to follow.

resolution.title: [redfish]: use unix socket for supervisor-proc-exit-listener CONFIG_DB access
resolution.description:
**What I did**

Add `--use-unix-socket-path` to `supervisor-proc-exit-listener` in `dockers/docker-sonic-redfish/supervisord.conf`.

**Why I did it**

Fixes #29245.

The `redfish` container is the only SONiC container that runs with `--net=bridge` (see [`files/build_templates/docker_image_ctl.j2#L699-L704`](https://github.com/sonic-net/sonic-buildimage/blob/master/files/build_templates/docker_image_ctl.j2#L699-L704)), because it uses `-p <IP>:443:18080` to remap the external HTTPS port.

As a consequence, `<IP>:6379` inside the container does not reach the host redis. `ConfigDBConnector().connect()` (TCP mode) fails with `RuntimeError: Unable to connect to redis - Connection refused`. `supervisor-proc-exit-listener`'s `get_autorestart_state()` catches that and returns `""`. Since `"" != "enabled"`, the listener never sends `SIGTERM` to supervisord when a critical process exits, so container teardown never happens, so container-level autorestart is effectively broken for redfish.

Every other SONiC container using this listener runs on `--net=host` and reaches redis over TCP, so they are unaffected. The `redfish` container already bind-mounts `/var/run/redis:/var/run/redis:rw`, so the unix socket is available; switching the listener to unix-socket mode is a one-line, redfish-only change.

**How I verified it**

Applied the equivalent change on a live SONiC BMC DUT (Chipmunk, `sonic-aspeed-arm64-20260810.06`):

- Before: `docker exec redfish kill -9 <sonic-dbus-bridge pid>` → supervisord respawns in place, container stays up indefinitely.
- After: same kill → container exits within 30s (`systemd[1]: redfish.service: Deactivated successfully`); systemd restarts the service; new container comes up clean and healthy. `autorestart/test_container_autorestart.py::test_containers_autorestart[...-redfish]` now behaves as designed.
